candidates.current_role: Comal ISD administrator; Republican nominee for Comal County Clerk
candidates.background: LeAnn Miller has lived in Comal County for 20 years and has worked for Comal Independent School District for 17 years, the last five as an administrator. She ran for county clerk after County Clerk Bobbie Koepp decided to retire, and won the March 2026 Republican primary. The county directory lists Koepp as the current county clerk.

priorities.text: Says she wants to make the clerk's office more efficient and spend its budget with taxpayers in mind.
Campaigns on friendly, efficient public service and modernizing the office.
Says she wants to educate residents about clerk services such as the county's property fraud system.

notes.text: The New Braunfels Herald-Zeitung reported that she won the March 2026 Republican primary with 67.97 percent of the vote.

candidates.current_role: Comal County Treasurer
candidates.background: Renee Couch is the Comal County Treasurer and is running unopposed for a sixth term. priorities.text: Describes the treasurer's role as the county's banker, working with the depository bank to safeguard county funds.

record.text: The Herald-Zeitung reported that during her tenure the office added a cash management coordinator position.

candidates.current_role: Rancher; New Braunfels ISD trustee; Republican nominee for Comal County Commissioner, Precinct 2
candidates.background: Steve Minus is a San Antonio native who attended the University of Texas at San Antonio on a baseball scholarship, played for the Boston Red Sox for about four years, and then worked about 20 years in construction sales and manufacturing. He has served on the New Braunfels ISD board for five years. He won the March 2026 Republican primary for the Precinct 2 seat held by Commissioner Scott Haag, who did not appear on the primary ballot.

priorities.text: Says he wants more public collaboration among stakeholders, describing the county as feeling segmented.

notes.text: The New Braunfels Herald-Zeitung reported that he won the March 2026 Republican primary with 51.36 percent of the vote.

issue_notes.summary: Says he is in full support of protecting property rights but that the requirements developers must meet are disjointed.

candidates.current_role: Comal County Commissioner, Precinct 4
candidates.background: Jen Crownover is the Comal County Commissioner for Precinct 4, according to the county directory, and has served nearly three terms. She is running unopposed for a fourth term. She says she entered county government through community work on county parks and infrastructure projects.

priorities.text: Says her focus has been improving county communication and transparency, including explaining which duties belong to the county, state or cities.
Holds weekly station days in Canyon Lake and Spring Branch to meet constituents.

record.text: Cites completion of the new county jail and remodeled sheriff's office and downtown court buildings during her tenure.

issue_notes.summary: Says she has pushed for a school zone on Loop 306 at Rebecca Creek.
